headline: Courage is not the absence of fear—it's action in spite of fear
universal_truth: The brave feel fear; they simply don't let it decide for them
fun_facts: Firefighters and soldiers report feeling intense fear—they act anyway because of training and purpose
The word courage comes from the Latin 'cor' meaning heart—courage was originally 'speaking one's mind with heart'
Research shows that acting brave actually makes you feel braver over time
discussion_questions: What's one thing you would do if you weren't afraid?
Who in your life shows quiet courage?
What fear have you overcome that once seemed impossible?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: We imagine heroes as fearless. But ask any firefighter running into a burning building, any soldier in combat, any parent facing a child's diagnosis—they'll tell you the same thing: they were terrified. So what is courage, really?

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: If courage isn't the absence of fear, then the bravest people feel fear just like the rest of us. What separates them? What makes someone act when every instinct screams to run?

options.text: A purpose or value stronger than the fear
options.response: Exactly. Courage comes when something matters more than our comfort.

options.text: Training that overrides the fear response
options.response: Training helps, but there's something even more fundamental...

q1.title: Fear Is Universal
q1.script: Studies of combat soldiers show that nearly all experience intense fear before and during battle. The difference? They've practiced acting despite it. Training doesn't eliminate fear—it builds the habit of moving through it.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Fear Is Universal"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: The Heart's Speech
q2.script: The word courage comes from the Latin 'cor'—heart. Originally, courage meant speaking your true mind, being who you really are. Physical bravery came later. The oldest courage is authenticity—being honest about who you are.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Brave Begets Brave
q3.script: Psychologists have found that acting courageous—even when you don't feel it—actually builds genuine courage. It's called the 'as if' principle. Behavior shapes feeling. The more you act brave, the braver you become.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Courage isn't a feeling you wait for. It's a decision you make. Fear will show up—let it come. Then do the thing anyway. That's the only way courage has ever worked.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 13. Tomorrow, we'll discover why curious people learn more than others. Until then, identify one small fear you could face today—and face it.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Courage Practice - One Small Fear
growTrack.learning_objective: Build courage through small deliberate actions
growTrack.activity: Identify one small thing that makes you uncomfortable—sending that email, having that conversation, trying something new. Do it today. Notice: the fear before is usually worse than the action itself.
